memory_update.text: Direct ABF film and AI package-substrate makers are mostly non-US primary listings or OTC ADRs; US-listed exposure is cleaner in process control, substrate inspection, advanced packaging metrology, plating chemistry and equipment.

ONTO should be tracked as an underfollowed AI package-substrate yield candidate because Firefly G3 and panel-level packaging tools explicitly target advanced IC substrates, HPC, AI, cloud and high-I/O integration.

CAMT should be tracked as an underfollowed AI advanced-packaging inspection candidate due to Hawk orders for AI applications and product exposure to HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding and very high micro-bump counts.

MKSI should be tracked as an obscure second-order substrate-capacity candidate through Atotech's plating chemistry, equipment, software and ABF-compatible fine-line package-substrate manufacturing tools.

For the advanced package substrates and ABF node, the investable US chokepoint may be less about owning the direct substrate makers and more about owning yield-enabling tools, inspection, metrology, plating, desmear, metallization and process-control vendors.

node: Advanced package substrates and ABF build-up film for AI accelerators
summary: This pass expands the US-listed universe around the ABF/package-substrate chokepoint. The most direct substrate and ABF-film leaders named in the supplied context are mostly non-US primary listings or OTC ADRs, so the cleaner US-listed discovery lane is second-order: inspection/metrology, panel-level packaging tools, IC-substrate process control, plating chemistry/equipment, and yield-enabling process vendors. The strongest US-listed candidates for this node are KLA, Onto Innovation, Camtek, and MKS Instruments/Atotech. KLA is a reference leader; Onto, Camtek, and MKS are more relevant to the underfollowed lane because they map to substrate yield, panel-level packaging, micro-bump/chiplet/HBM inspection, ABF-compatible plating, and fine-line substrate manufacturing rather than headline GPU design.
